site.name: migration-atlas
site.summary: Migration Atlas — animal migration tracking (local demo) Fictional global animal-tracking atlas. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly. Page `index.html` — Atlas Three columns: left filter rail, center map + player, right inspector. The map is a hand-rolled SVG world (equirectangular projection) drawn from inline continent polygons and lon/lat graticules. Seven species are pre-loaded, each with a per-individual synthetic track of 12 monthly waypoints. Filters (left): species toggles with sample size counts, study year, display toggles (trail line, monthly position dots, stop-over polygons). Player (below map): slider scrubs through January → December. Play / pause button animates the season; speed selector controls cadence. As the slider advances, individuals' trails extend.

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full migration-atlas system, prioritizing the primary data visualization flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Migration Atlas provides a functional data visualization flow with responsive filtering and timeline controls, but suffers from significant accessibility and feedback gaps. Critical issues include undersized touch targets for mobile users (13x13px checkboxes), missing system feedback for 'Save' and 'Cite' actions, and state synchronization failures in the 'Study Year' filter. Additionally, core drill-down interactions on the map frequently fail due to unresponsive SVG elements.

exploration_plan.goal: Validate the core data visualization flow of the Migration Atlas, specifically focusing on the interaction between filters, the timeline player, and the map rendering, while assessing mobile usability given identified layout risks.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will proceed by first establishing a baseline view with default filters, then systematically manipulating the timeline (scrubbing and playing) to verify SVG trail updates. Subsequently, it will test filter logic (species toggles, year selection) and display options. Finally, it will validate the 'Individual' inspector panel interactions and repeat critical checks on a mobile viewport to address known tap-target issues.
assumptions: The application is a Single Page Application (SPA) or local fixture where navigation links ('Studies', 'About') may trigger modals or scroll-to-sections rather than full page reloads.
SVG map elements (trails, dots) are interactive and linked to the 'Individual' inspector panel on the right.
The 'Play' button initiates an automatic interval that advances the month slider.
risk_hotspots: Mobile Viewport: High density of small tap targets (checkboxes, nav links) flagged in prescan.
Timeline Player: Synchronization between the slider position, the 'Current Month' header, and the visible SVG trails.
Filter Logic: Ensuring unchecking a species immediately removes its corresponding trails from the map without breaking the renderer.
Inspector Panel: Verifying that clicking a specific trail updates the right-hand panel with correct individual stats.

phases.title: Baseline & Timeline Mechanics
phases.objective: Verify the default state renders correctly and the primary time-navigation controls function as expected.
key_checks: Confirm initial load shows '2025 season' and 'May' as current month.
Scrub the month slider manually from Jan to Dec and observe trail extension/retraction.
Click 'Play' and verify the slider advances automatically; click 'Pause' to stop.
Change playback speed (0.5x, 2x, 4x) and observe cadence change.
exit_criteria: Slider moves smoothly across all months.
Map trails visually update in sync with the selected month.
Play/Pause/Speed controls respond without console errors.

phases.title: Filtering & Display Logic
phases.objective: Validate that left-rail filters correctly isolate data subsets and toggle visual layers.
key_checks: Toggle 'Western osprey' off; verify its trails disappear from the map and count drops.
Use 'Filter species...' input to search for 'turtle'; verify only Leatherback remains.
Switch 'Study Year' to '2024' and '2026'; verify map data resets/updates accordingly.
Toggle 'Show trail', 'Show monthly positions', and 'Show stop-over polygons' individually to verify layer visibility.
exit_criteria: Species counts in the legend update dynamically.
Display toggles show/hide specific SVG elements without layout shift.

phases.title: Inspector & Interaction Flow
phases.objective: Test the drill-down capability from the global map to individual animal details.
key_checks: Click on a visible trail or dot on the map.
Verify the 'Individual' panel on the right populates with specific data (ID, stats).
Check if the selected individual is highlighted on the map while others dim (if applicable).
Attempt to 'Save view' and 'Cite this view' to check for modal dialogs or copy-to-clipboard actions.
exit_criteria: Inspector panel updates contextually based on map selection.

phases.title: Mobile Usability & Navigation
phases.objective: Assess the interface on a mobile viewport, focusing on the high-risk small tap targets identified in the prescan.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport (e.g., iPhone SE or Pixel 5).
Attempt to toggle a species checkbox (verify if hit-area is sufficient despite small visual size).
Test the month slider scrubbing on touch.
Check if the three-column layout collapses into a stacked or tabbed view.
Verify top navigation links are clickable.
exit_criteria: Core functionality (filtering, playing timeline) is accessible on mobile.
Identify any completely unusable controls due to overlap or size.

coverage_targets.features: All inputs (checkboxes, sliders, selects), buttons (play, save, cite), and map interactions.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat Phase 1 and Phase 2 key checks on mobile viewport.

notes: Since this is a local fixture, network error checking is low priority unless external assets (fonts/images) fail to load.
Pay close attention to the 'Monarch butterfly' entry which notes 'swarm aggregate'—this may render differently than individual tracks.
If 'Studies' or 'About' links do not navigate, check if they open hidden sections or modals within the DOM.

findings.user_goal: Filter species and adjust display settings on a mobile device.
findings.problem: Interactive checkboxes for species filters and display toggles are significantly smaller than recommended mobile touch targets (13x13px vs 44x44px).
findings.evidence: Layout warnings in steps-37-42 and final_observation identify multiple inputs (e.g., ux-4 'Western osprey', ux-12 'Show trail') with dimensions of 13x13px. While the agent managed to click them, this represents high friction and error risk for human users.
findings.why_it_matters: Users will experience difficulty selecting filters on touchscreens, leading to frustration and accidental selections. This violates basic mobile accessibility guidelines.
findings.suggestion: Increase the clickable area of all checkboxes and toggles to at least 44x44px, using CSS padding or pseudo-elements if the visual checkbox size must remain small.

findings.user_goal: Save the current view configuration or cite the data source.
findings.problem: Clicking 'Save view' and 'Cite this view' buttons produces no visible user feedback (no modal, toast, or download).
findings.evidence: In steps-13-18 and steps-37-42, the agent clicked these buttons (ux-1, ux-2) but observed no UI change, modal appearance, or clipboard confirmation. The action appeared to do nothing.
findings.why_it_matters: Lack of system status visibility leaves users uncertain if their action succeeded. They may repeatedly click the button or assume the feature is broken.
findings.suggestion: Implement immediate feedback such as a toast notification ('View saved'), a modal dialog for citation details, or a file download trigger.
findings.source_hint: steps-13-18: ux_signals regarding 'Cite this view'; steps-37-42: ux_signals regarding 'Save view'

findings.user_goal: Inspect specific migration data by clicking on an individual animal's trail or label.
findings.problem: Clicking on map labels (e.g., 'CAR-52', 'MON-90') and trails frequently fails to trigger the 'Individual' inspector panel.
findings.evidence: Multiple failures recorded in steps-01-06, steps-13-18, and steps-19-24 (e.g., 'Click failed for ux-map-label-car47'). The inspector panel often remains in the default 'Click a trail...' state despite visible map elements.
findings.why_it_matters: This blocks the primary analytical workflow of the application. Users cannot access detailed data for specific individuals, rendering the visualization superficial.
findings.suggestion: Debug SVG event handling and z-index issues. Ensure hit areas for trails and labels are sufficiently large and that click events properly propagate to update the inspector state.

findings.user_goal: Change the dataset year to compare migration patterns across different seasons.
findings.problem: The 'Study Year' dropdown updates locally but fails to synchronize with the main application header and map data.
findings.evidence: In steps-07-12 and steps-19-24, the agent selected '2024 season' in the filter rail, but the main header remained 'Migration Atlas — 2025 season' and map stats did not update accordingly.
findings.why_it_matters: Users are misled into thinking they are viewing a different year's data when they are not. This creates a trust gap and potential for data misinterpretation.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the global application state (header title, map layers, aggregate stats) updates immediately and visibly when the 'Study Year' filter is changed.
findings.source_hint: steps-07-12: ux_signals ('main dashboard header still displays... 2025 season')

findings.user_goal: Navigate the interface using assistive technologies or understand form context.
findings.problem: The 'Study Year' select dropdown lacks an associated accessible label.
findings.evidence: Final observation layout warning identifies ux-11 (the year selector) as having 'no label, aria-label, or placeholder'.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will hear 'combo box' without context, making it unclear what the dropdown controls.
findings.suggestion: Add a visible <label> element linked to the select input, or add an aria-label attribute describing the control (e.g., 'Select Study Year').

gaps: 5 browser action(s) failed and should be retried or analyzed.
